# Comment templates
Load when: you write a progress, stale, blocker, dependency-release, done-check or closure comment on an activity
Applies to: lpm-deliver-activity, lpm-plan-work, lpm-unblock-work    Source: legacy `software-project-orchestrator` operating templates; process rules (pilot pattern, Evidence); card `create_comment`
Owner skill: lpm-deliver-activity

## Summary
- Comments are the activity's history: one comment per event, in the user's language, at most 20,000 characters.
- Every comment carries an `idempotencyKey` built from the event (recipes below).
- State the concrete risk or result; never a generic reminder.
- Prefer a comment for activity-local follow-up and a notification for deadline, blocker or ownership escalation; send both only when the item is both stale and time-critical.

## Facts
| Template | Use when | idempotencyKey |
|---|---|---|
| Progress | after commits or tests on the activity | `progress-<issueId>-<yyyymmdd>-<n>` |
| Stale | `in-progress` and no update or comment for more than 48 h | `stale-<issueId>-<yyyymmdd>` |
| Blocker | the activity cannot move and the cause is unclear | `blocker-<issueId>-<yyyymmdd>` |
| Dependency release | an upstream blocker was resolved | `release-<upstreamIssueId>-<issueId>` |
| Done check | before closing an activity that blocked others or has follow-ups | `donecheck-<issueId>` |
| Closure | the closure check passed | `close-<issueId>` |
| Scope reduction | the activity is at risk for the current cycle | `scope-<issueId>-<cycleId>` |

## Rules
1. Fill every `<placeholder>` from tool results or your own run; delete lines that do not apply instead of writing "n/a". The examples use Portuguese labels: translate the labels to the user's language.
2. Link commits by SHA and evidence by attachment id; never paste secrets or long logs (attach them).
3. A closure comment names the pending item when one exists, and then the activity stays open.
4. Discussion of an activity stays in its comments; governance threads cannot target activities.

## Examples
```text
example: Progress
Progresso: <what changed, one line>
Commits: <sha7> <subject>; <sha7> <subject>
Testes: <command> -> <passed/failed counts>
Pendente: <none | item>
Próximo passo: <one action>
```
```text
example: Stale
Sem atualização há <hours> h (desde <date>).
Risco: <what slips if it stays stopped, e.g. milestone <name> on <date>>
Pergunta para <assignee>: <blocker | pending decision | scope change>?
```
```text
example: Blocker
Bloqueio: <cause, one line> — desbloqueia: <who> — desde <date>
Depende de: <upstream issueId | linkId | decision threadId>
Próximo passo: <action>, por <who>
```
```text
example: Dependency release
Liberado: <upstreamIssueId> (<status>) não bloqueia mais <issueId> (link <linkId>).
Próximo passo: <action>, por <who>
```
```text
example: Done check
Antes de concluir <issueId>: dependentes <issueIds | none>; bloqueios ativos <none | linkIds>.
Follow-up separado: <new issueId | none>
```
```text
example: Scope reduction
Em risco no ciclo <cycle name> (termina <date>): <remaining work> vs <capacity>.
Proposta: <smaller deliverable>; resto em <new issueId | next cycle>. Decide: <who>
```
```text
example: Closure (pilot pattern)
Correção: <what was fixed>
Teste reproduzível: <command or steps> -> <result>
Evidência registrada: <fileName> (<attachmentId>), <fileName> (<attachmentId>)
Resultado: <approved by <who> | pending: <specific item>, owner <who>>
Próximo passo: <one action>
```
